adapters.limitation: Matches patterns a rule encodes; it does not prove the absence of the vulnerability class, and silent rule drift looks identical to a clean repository.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'brew install gitleaks'
adapters.limitation: Detects credential shapes, not validity: it cannot tell a live secret from a revoked or fabricated one, and it says nothing about whether the processing is lawful.

adapters.install: download the v3 release binary from GitHub
adapters.limitation: Verification only covers providers with a verifier implemented; an unverifiable or internal credential is reported as unverified or not at all, and history rewriting hides nothing already leaked.

adapters.install: download the v2 release binary from GitHub, or 'go install github.com/google/osv-scanner/v2/cmd/osv-scanner@latest'
adapters.limitation: Resolves declared dependencies against published advisories; it is blind to vendored or patched code, to private packages, and to any vulnerability that has no advisory yet.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'brew install trivy'
adapters.limitation: Depends on feed freshness and on the package metadata inside the image; most base-image findings are not fixable in this repository, so an unfiltered run trains reviewers to ignore it.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'brew install syft'
adapters.limitation: Records composition only. An SBOM proves neither vulnerability status nor license compliance, and a component the cataloger cannot parse is simply absent from the list.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'brew install grype'
adapters.limitation: Only as complete as the SBOM it reads and the vulnerability database it last downloaded; it does not decide whether the vulnerable path is reachable from your code.
Checks declared infrastructure, never deployed state; drift applied after the last plan, and anything provisioned outside these files, is invisible.
Syntactic patterns over Python AST nodes; it has no data-flow model, so it misses tainted input reaching a sink and flags safe constructs that merely look dangerous.
Enforces the configured rule set on parseable files. It proves style and a narrow class of defects, never that the behaviour is correct, and disabled rules leave no trace in a green run.
Fast lexical and AST linting only; it says nothing about runtime behaviour, and a per-file 'noqa' silences a rule where it mattered most.
Proves internal type consistency of annotated code. Untyped modules, 'Any' at a boundary and runtime data from the network are outside the proof.
Proves the assertions that were written. A green suite bounds nothing about untested paths, and coverage percentage measures execution, not assertion.
Proves the assertions that were written, under mocks that the same author chose; a mock that drifts from the real dependency keeps passing forever.
Same bound as any unit runner: the suite proves the asserted behaviour of the code as loaded in the test environment, not the behaviour of the deployed artifact.
A mutation score measures test strength, not correctness: surviving mutants need triage, equivalent mutants can never be killed, and the run costs orders of magnitude more than the suite it grades.
Only as good as the schema: a wrong-but-well-formed response passes, and conformance to the contract is not business correctness.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'brew install k6'
adapters.limitation: Measures saturation in one environment with one dataset. It proves nothing about fault injection, dependency loss, recovery time, or production capacity with cold caches and noisy neighbours.
The load shape is whatever the script models; a synthetic arrival pattern that never matches production traffic produces a number nobody can act on.

adapters.install: pip install presidio-analyzer presidio-anonymizer, then write the scan entry point; presidio ships as a library and a service, not as a repository scanner
adapters.limitation: Recall depends on locale and on the entity recognisers enabled; it cannot see personal data assembled at runtime, and it never decides whether the processing has a lawful basis.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'cargo install lychee'
adapters.limitation: Proves that a URL answered at scan time. It cannot see that the page now says something different, and rate limits or offline runs turn into false failures.

adapters.install: download the release binary from GitHub, or 'brew install hadolint'
adapters.limitation: Lints Dockerfile instructions against known rules; it does not inspect the resulting image, its packages, or what the entrypoint actually runs.
